When a pruned reasoning model undergoes reinforcement learning, one pruning criterion can achieve 4.4 times the peak reward of another, yet both recover to the same downstream accuracy. This phenomenon, which we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}, challenges the assumption that RL-based recovery universally outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for compressed reasoning models.
We propose Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), which scores candidate structures by combining gradient importance with representational diversity measured through Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA). Applied to a 7B reasoning model, four pruning criteria produce qualitatively different RL outcomes, from active learning through stagnation to complete reward collapse. We call this gradient a \emph{recovery capacity spectrum}. Yet at moderate sparsity, SFT and RL yield near-identical accuracy across all criteria.
These findings suggest that SFT warmup captures most recoverable reasoning capacity, while RL training exposes structural differences between pruning strategies without converting them into accuracy gains. Directional trends are consistent across three benchmarks, with preliminary cross-scale and cross-model evidence\footnote{Code and data are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/recovery_aware_struct_prune-5FA5/}.}.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Structured pruning compresses reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) by removing entire groups of feed-forward channels, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
A natural question is which recovery paradigm to use.
Recent work gives a clear answer: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) substantially outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy~\citep{selfhealing2025}.
This hierarchy creates a testable prediction: a pruning criterion that better preserves the model's ability to benefit from RL should yield higher accuracy after recovery.

Our experiments challenge this prediction.
On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{deepseek2025r1} pruned to 20\% MLP channel sparsity, one criterion achieves 4.4 times the peak RL reward of another under GRPO~\citep{shao2024grpo}, yet all criteria recover to within 1 percentage point of the same downstream accuracy.
The pruning criterion shapes RL training dynamics profoundly: it determines whether the model learns, stagnates, or exhibits reward collapse.
But it has minimal effect on final task performance.
Since RL optimizes reward as a proxy for accuracy, this disconnect is unexpected.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_dose_response.pdf}
\caption{Dose-response curve for the CKA diversity coefficient $\alpha$ at 20\% MLP channel sparsity on GSM8K ($N{=}1{,}319$). Recovery accuracy follows an inverted-U, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). SFT and GRPO curves nearly overlap ($|\Delta| \leq 1.14$\,pp at every point), illustrating reward-accuracy decoupling.}
\label{fig:dose_response}
\end{figure}

The surprise deepens when viewed through a mechanistic lens.
RL compresses incorrect reasoning paths while SFT expands correct ones~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}.
These asymmetric pressures predict that the two paradigms should complement each other, not converge to the same outcome.
Yet existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for immediate post-pruning quality without examining how the criterion shapes RL recovery.
No prior work has compared multiple criteria under RL or tested whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.
\citet{selfhealing2025} evaluate unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% parameter retention; our structural removal of entire channel groups may impose different demands on recovery.

We investigate through Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), a scoring function that combines gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity~\citep{kornblith2019cka}.
A single coefficient $\alpha$ controls the balance (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}): the dose-response curve reveals an inverted-U in recovery accuracy, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K;~\citealp{cobbe2021gsm8k}).
Under GRPO, four criteria produce a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum}, from active learning (CKA-only, 4.4$\times$ peak reward) to complete reward collapse (\rasp{} at $\alpha{=}1.0$), that tracks preserved diversity rather than importance.
Yet at every point on this spectrum, SFT and GRPO yield near-identical accuracy (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}), a pattern we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}.
A depth pruning baseline (ShortGPT;~\citealp{shortgpt2024}) is the sole exception ($-$1.36\,pp on GSM8K), which suggests that pruning granularity interacts with RL trainability.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Reward-accuracy decoupling.} At 20--25\% fine-grained MLP sparsity, SFT and GRPO yield equivalent accuracy regardless of pruning criterion, confirmed by TOST equivalence testing. At 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage, which delineates the boundary of this phenomenon (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
    \item \textbf{Recovery capacity spectrum.} \rasp{} reveals that four pruning criteria produce qualitatively distinct RL dynamics. Dose-response analysis traces an inverted-U in recovery, with preliminary evidence across scales and model families (\S\ref{sec:scoring}, \S\ref{sec:recovery_gradient}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_method_framework.pdf}
\caption{Overview of our pruning comparison framework. \textbf{Left}: structural analysis computes importance $I(h)$ and CKA-based overlap $F(h)$ scores, which four scoring criteria combine differently (Eqs.~\ref{eq:standard}--\ref{eq:cka_only}). \textbf{Center}: ranked structures are removed up to the target sparsity, subject to per-layer capacity floors. \textbf{Right}: all pruned models undergo identical two-stage recovery (SFT warmup $\to$ GRPO). \textbf{Bottom}: the resulting recovery capacity spectrum, from active learning (CKA-only) to reward collapse (\rasp{} at $\alpha{=}1.0$), tracks preserved representational diversity rather than gradient importance.}
\label{fig:method_framework}
\end{figure*}

1	When a pruned reasoning model undergoes reinforcement learning, one pruning criterion can achieve 4.4 times the peak reward of another, yet both recover to the same downstream accuracy. This phenomenon, which we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}, challenges the assumption that RL-based recovery universally outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for compressed reasoning models.
2	We propose Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), which scores candidate structures by combining gradient importance with representational diversity measured through Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA). Applied to a 7B reasoning model, four pruning criteria produce qualitatively different RL outcomes, from active learning through stagnation to complete reward collapse. We call this gradient a \emph{recovery capacity spectrum}. Yet at moderate sparsity, SFT and RL yield near-identical accuracy across all criteria.
3	These findings suggest that SFT warmup captures most recoverable reasoning capacity, while RL training exposes structural differences between pruning strategies without converting them into accuracy gains. Directional trends are consistent across three benchmarks, with preliminary cross-scale and cross-model evidence\footnote{Code and data are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/recovery_aware_struct_prune-5FA5/}.}.
